reason_for_lift: 570 is the smallest positive multiple of 114 reached by an integer lift that is divisible by 5, activating the 5-standard family used in the published two-pair theorem.

enumeration.method: additive-hash meet-in-the-middle with exact full-unit-profile verification; hashing can add false candidates but cannot remove a true complementary profile
enumeration.calibration: same enumerator reproduces the exact prior m=110 grade-2 count 1648

lattice_filter.published_generator_family: Aoki S_m pair vectors plus all prime-standard vectors, p=2 included

result: No grade-2 Hodge quadruple at level 570 satisfies even the necessary mod-2 quotient condition for lying in the lifted W114 target coset. Therefore no two-pair-standard coset-transfer witness exists for this 5-lift.
strength: The zero mod-2-syndrome count is already decisive; it does not depend on the later integer-lattice reducer for excluding candidates.
combined_two_pair_boundary: Base W70@70, W110@110, certified lifts W70@210 and W110@220, and the minimal 5-activating lift W114@570 all fail the necessary grade-2 same-coset condition for the published two-pair closure route.
claim_ceiling: Mechanism-specific obstruction only. Other lifts, algebraic gap families, correspondences, exchange families, or new geometric constructions remain open. This is not a non-algebraicity result and uses no P-vs-NP evidence.
